title: Reading Corner Newsletter on Decoding Skills
source_title: Kramer Elementary | Smore Newsletters for Education

blocks.content: Title Talk Reading Corner February NewsletterWhat does decoding mean? A simple definition for decoding is recognizing letter sounds or patterns and blending them together to translate a written word into speech. Decoding is a foundational reading skill (phonics) that must be developed to begin successful reading with fluency. This process begins with students recognizing their letters and sounds then blending the sounds to speak the word, i.e., /c/ - /a/ - /t/ becomes cat.Here is an example of what happens when a student decodes a word:Recognizing letters and letter patterns (like b, sh, igh)Knowing the sounds they makeBlending those sounds together to read a wordActivities: Reading Rockets is a reputable research-based website for all things reading; and below are age-specific resources for decoding activities.Kindergarten: https://www.readingrockets.org/literacy-home/reading-101Kindergartener phonics and decoding activitiesFirst Grade:https://www.readingrockets.org/literacy-home/reading-101-guide-parents/your-first-grader/phonics-and-decoding-activitiesSecond Grade:https://www.readingrockets.org/literacy-home/reading-101-guide-parents/your-second-grader/phonics-and-decoding-activitiesThird Grade:Here is a video showing how a 3rd grade student uses syllables to decode longer words more easily.Questions or need help? Please reach out to your child's Reading Corner instructor; Mrs. Geshan, geshanc@talawanda.org, Mrs. Kobermann, kobermanc@talawanda.org, or Mrs. Walters, waltersh@talawanda.org.

summary: The February **Reading Corner Newsletter** explains decoding—the foundational reading skill of recognizing letter sounds and blending them to read words. The newsletter provides **grade-specific decoding activities** for Kindergarten through 3rd grade via Reading Rockets website links, including a video showing how 3rd graders use syllables to decode longer words. Parents can contact Mrs. Geshan (geshanc@talawanda.org), Mrs. Kobermann (kobermanc@talawanda.org), or Mrs. Walters (waltersh@talawanda.org) with questions.

title: Principal's Weekly Update from Marshall
source_title: Marshall E-News | Smore Newsletters for Education

blocks.content: It has been a great week at Marshall! Students were engaged, kind, and eager to learn. From strong academic focus to positive interactions across grade levels, our students continue to show what it means to be respectful, responsible, and ready to learn.We are proud of the way students are supporting one another—whether through classroom collaboration, peer helping, or simply being good friends. Thank you for reinforcing these values at home; your partnership truly makes a difference.Thank you for all you do to support Marshall. We are grateful to work alongside such a caring and supportive community. We look forward to another great week ahead!Mrs. Jones, Principal

summary: Principal Mrs. Jones celebrates a successful week at Marshall, highlighting students' strong academic engagement and positive behavior. Students demonstrated respect, responsibility, and readiness to learn through classroom collaboration, peer helping, and supportive friendships. The principal thanks families for reinforcing these values at home and looks forward to another great week.
